Messages.Author: Michael Gerdau
Messages.Body:
Dear fellow Methuselah !

a week ago when testng my new Brujah deck my group ran into the
following questions:

1) Donal O'Connor is blocked. Combat starts and opposing vamp looses
1 blood due to Donal's special ability. Combat ends, Donal plays
Psyche to start a new combat. Does the opposing vamp loose another
1 blood before this 2. combat starts ?

I clained yes (we agreed to rule no for the time being) and the
argument is that Donal did not perform a new action but it is just
a new combat that starts since his action was blocked in the first
place and therefor qualifies for the bloodloss.

That leads to another question (has been asked in the past but don't
remember the answer):
If during this 2. combat Donal plays Form of Mist (he's got sup PRO :-)
would he be allowed to continue his action 2 combats ago ?

I'd say yes (but you never know :-)

2) Bianca (with sup POT) played Fists of Death and Undead Strength to
hit the opposing vamp (4 blood) for 6 thus sending her to topor.
Bianca then played Taste of Vitae. How much blood did she get.
4 or 6 ?
(We agreed on 4 but I rather would have seen 6 :-)

Michael

Messages.Author: R. Brian Smith
Messages.Body:
In article <qdnsxoea...@elmshorn.netsurf.de>,
michael...@elmshorn.netsurf.de wrote:

> Dear fellow Methuselah !
>
> a week ago when testng my new Brujah deck my group ran into the
> following questions:
>
> 1) Donal O'Connor is blocked. Combat starts and opposing vamp looses
> 1 blood due to Donal's special ability. Combat ends, Donal plays
> Psyche to start a new combat. Does the opposing vamp loose another
> 1 blood before this 2. combat starts ?

Actually it is no. Donal was only blocked once. He decided to re-start the
combat, not perform a second action.

Even if you consider re-starting a successful action (which you really
shouldn't) the action always succeeds. Thus no blood loss

> That leads to another question (has been asked in the past but don't
> remember the answer):
> If during this 2. combat Donal plays Form of Mist (he's got sup PRO :-)
> would he be allowed to continue his action 2 combats ago ?

I believe so, but if I am wrong then I will be corrected

>
> 2) Bianca (with sup POT) played Fists of Death and Undead Strength to
> hit the opposing vamp (4 blood) for 6 thus sending her to topor.
> Bianca then played Taste of Vitae. How much blood did she get.
> 4 or 6 ?
> (We agreed on 4 but I rather would have seen 6 :-)

4. You can only gain blood for the amount of blood lost due to damage, not
the amount of damage dealt.

Good luck!

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
tam...@nurk.com (R. Brian Smith) writes:

>In article <qdnsxoea...@elmshorn.netsurf.de>,
>michael...@elmshorn.netsurf.de wrote:

>> Dear fellow Methuselah !
>>
>> a week ago when testng my new Brujah deck my group ran into the
>> following questions:
>>
>> 1) Donal O'Connor is blocked. Combat starts and opposing vamp looses
>> 1 blood due to Donal's special ability. Combat ends, Donal plays
>> Psyche to start a new combat. Does the opposing vamp loose another
>> 1 blood before this 2. combat starts ?

>Actually it is no. Donal was only blocked once. He decided to re-start the
>combat, not perform a second action.

With the current errata, that's correct. But, as written, Donal would
have required the blocker to pay an additional blood before the second
combat. (Now, Donal just forces the blocker to burn a blood as the
action is blocked - combat or no - so a second combat wouldn't invoke
his special ability).

----
And that leads to more questions (TOM):
Does the current errata/ruling on Donal mean that, if Donal untaps
with Change of Target, the blocker still pays one (since the one
is burned when the action is blocked - not during combat).
Similarly, the blocker would burn 1 even if he used Obedience to
avoid combat, right?
